title: Today's 'Renewals due' counts a plan that has not started yet, while 'plans end this week' on the same screen leaves it out
what: A short plan sold to start later (a weekly plan or day pass starting tomorrow, say) that ends within the next 7 days is counted in the Renewals due tile and its list. The 'Messages to send' card on the same Today screen, the plans-ending message list and the assistant only count plans that cover today, so they leave this member out. The owner sees two different numbers for plans ending this week, and the Remind them list misses someone the tile counts.
expected: Both places use one rule for 'ends this week': either both count a plan that starts later and ends inside the week, or neither does.
how_often: whenever a plan that starts later ends within 7 days
fix_line: Make the Renewals tile and the plans-ending card share one ending-soon rule

title: Cancelling a plan or a receipt rewrites the whole Fees due line, so a drop or rise never shows and no reason is given
what: The Fees due tile works out every past point of its line, and the 'before' figure, using today's state of plans and receipts. When a plan with money owed is cancelled, its dues vanish from today's figure and from every past day too, so the tile says the same as before and the line stays flat: the owner never sees that money was written off. A receipt cancelled today pushes the whole past line up instead, as if the gym had always been owed it.
expected: Past points show what was owed on that day; a fall caused by a cancelled plan, or a rise caused by a cancelled receipt, shows on the line with a short reason.
how_often: every time a plan with dues or a receipt is cancelled
fix_line: Read past days with the cancel and void dates, and name write-offs under the tile

evidence: data-count: Crispy Curves crm_records 3 members (1 pass, joined 14-25 Nov), 2 year plans, 0 ending within 7 days, 0 archived, 0 future-start plans: tile, card and summary agree here but the data holds none of the edge cases, so the recount proves nothing
